A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICRL prompting framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated prompt examples and the renumbered abstract-generation figure.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, reward/context/prompt ablations, and unseen-paper abstract-generation results in Sections 5–6 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v5 retains those original empirical results and adds a controlled attention-head analysis in Section 6 and Appendix C.2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, experience-buffer construction, scalar feedback, and preset/autonomous exploration–exploitation prompting are unchanged. The new reward-label perturbations are diagnostic controls, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Game of 24, creative writing, ScienceWorld, AIME, HMMT, and unseen-paper abstract generation. The new attention probe reuses creative-writing trajectories; its reward-label manipulation introduces an analysis control within retained task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership within the corresponding benchmark and abstract-generation experiments is unchanged, including CoT/Long-CoT, Best-of-N, Self-Refine, Reflexion, and ScienceWorld's ReAct comparator. The all-1 reward prompt in Appendix C.2 is an internal diagnostic control.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a focused probing protocol: five trials from each of 100 creative-writing questions, paired prompts with randomized 1/10 versus all-1 rewards, and attention measurements across Qwen3-32B's last 32 layers. Existing benchmark evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 adds a controlled investigation of whether changing reward labels affects individual attention heads, substantially extending the analysis from behavioral diagnostics to model internals. Section 6 and Appendix C.2 report positive/negative reward sensitivity and depth-dependent patterns. Existing ablations and abstract-generation analysis are retained.

E5.justification: The new probe introduces per-head Pearson-correlation tests at nominal p < 0.05 across 2,048 heads and comparison against a 5% chance expectation. Existing cross-task standard-error reporting is unchanged. No multiple-testing adjustment or repeated-randomization uncertainty is described.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and all retained result curves are unchanged. Appendix C.2 newly reports 597 significant heads: 249 positively and 348 negatively correlated with reward labels. Its stated layer-group averages, 29.7 and 12.2, disagree with Figure 16's plotted counts, which average approximately 28.8 and 12.7.

T1.justification: The MDP, in-context policy, and token-generation mathematical formulations are unchanged. Neither version adds formal guarantees or proofs; the new attention correlations are empirical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about emergent inference-time RL, scalar-reward self-improvement, broad applicability, and advantages over self-revision methods. The attention study supplies additional support without redefining those core claims.

C2.justification: v5 adds interpretations of positively and negatively correlated heads as tracking successes and failures, with specialization across layers and an analogy to classical RL. Because the probe randomizes reward labels, its evidence directly supports label sensitivity more clearly than learning from actual successes or failures.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 documents the new probe's computation: averaging attention over each trial's response tokens, subtracting the matched all-1 baseline, pooling 500 observations per head, and indexing layers relative to the output. Existing prompt examples, implementation disclosures, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 4's research positioning and the cited-work set are unchanged. Removed webpage dates and shortened bibliographic metadata do not remove cited works or change the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v5 renames the learning-versus-search paragraph, adds the attention-analysis paragraph and Appendix C.2, and adds acknowledgments, supervising-author information, and publication headers. The existing prose and overall section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v5 adds Figure 16's stacked per-layer attention-head counts and chance reference line. The unchanged abstract-generation plot becomes Figure 17 and moves to the final page. Appendix A prompt figures are rearranged, with additional header and text-flow changes; existing tables and plots retain their displays.

improvement.justification: The controlled attention probe adds useful evidence that reward labels affect internal processing, supplementing v2's behavioral evidence with a documented diagnostic. Its contribution is limited by interpreting randomized labels as successes/failures and by the layer-average discrepancies in Appendix C.2. The aggregate counts and qualitative depth trend remain supported, so the addition provides a modest net benefit while leaving the central RL-mechanism interpretation unresolved.
